source_text:
Στίχ. δ΄. (10) Οὐ ποιήσεις σεαυτῷ εἴδωλον. Ἄλλο εἴδωλον, καὶ ἕτερον ὁμοίωμα. Ὁμοίωμα γάρ ἐστιν, ἐὰν ποιῇς ἰχθύος ἢ τετραπόδου, ἢ θηρίου, ἢ διὰ τεχνουργίας ἢ διὰ ζωγραφίας ὁμοίωμα· εἴδωλον δὲ, ὅσα ἀνατυποῦσα ψυχὴ ποιεῖ ἐξ οὐχ ὑπαρχόντων πρωτοτύπως· οἷον, ἀναμεμιγμένον τι ζῶον ἀπὸ ἀνθρώπου καὶ ἵππου.
Στίχ. δ΄ Ὅσα ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἄνω, καὶ ὅσα ἐν τῇ γῇ κάτω. καὶ ὅσα ἐν τοῖς ὕδασιν ὑποκάτω τῆς γῆς. Οὐ προσκυνήσεις αὐτοῖς, οὐδὲ μὴ λατρεύσεις αὐτοῖς.
Ἄλλο προσκυνεῖν, καὶ ἄλλο λατρεύειν. Ὁ μὲν γὰρ ἐξ ὅλης ψυχῆς δουλεύων τούτοις οὐ μόνον προσκυνεῖ. ἀλλὰ καὶ λατρεύει· ὁ δὲ καθυποκρινόμενος, καὶ δια τὰ ἔθη ποιῶν, οὐ λατρεύει μὲν, προσκυνεῖ δέ. Εὑρήσεις δὲ τοιούτους ἐν τοῖς Ἀριθμοῖς χαριζομένους γυναιξὶ, καὶ εἴδωλα προσκυνοῦντας.
thought_title: Idol versus likeness; bowing versus serving
orientation: Origen is commenting on Exodus 20:4-5, explaining the difference between an idol and a likeness, and between bowing down and serving.
pass_a_gloss: Verse 4. (10) You shall not make for yourself an idol. An idol is one thing, and a likeness is another. For it is a likeness, if you make of a fish or of a four-footed animal, or of a beast, either through craftsmanship or through painting a likeness; but an idol is whatever things the soul, forming an image, makes from things not existing in an original way; for example, some mixed animal from a human and a horse. Verse 4. Whatever things are in the heaven above, and whatever things are on the earth below, and whatever things are in the waters under the earth. You shall not bow down to them, nor shall you serve them. Bowing down is one thing, and serving is another. For the one who serves these things from the whole soul not only bows down, but also serves; but the one who plays the hypocrite, and does things because of customs, does not serve, but bows down. And you will find such men in Numbers gratifying women, and bowing down to idols.

choices.why: Glossary term; an image formed by the soul from things that have no original existence.
Glossary term; a likeness made by art or painting of an existing creature.
Glossary term; to prostrate oneself or bow down in worship, which may be done hypocritically.
Glossary term; to serve with the whole soul, indicating full inward devotion.
Captures the pretense of outward worship without inward devotion, matching the contrast with serving from the whole soul.

choices.english: from things not existing in an original way
choices.why: Literal rendering of the philosophical distinction: the idol's source has no original existence.
rejected: from things that do not exist originally

pass_b_english: "You shall not make for yourself an idol" (Exodus 20:4). An idol is one thing, and a likeness is another. For it is a likeness if you make a likeness of a fish or a four-footed animal or a beast, whether by craftsmanship or by painting. But an idol is whatever the soul forms as an image and makes from things that do not exist in an original way—for example, a mixed creature from a human and a horse.
"Whatever is in heaven above, and whatever is on the earth below, and whatever is in the waters under the earth. You shall not bow down to them, nor shall you serve them" (Exodus 20:5).

Bowing down is one thing, and serving is another. For the one who serves these things from the whole soul does not only bow down but also serves. But the one who plays the hypocrite and acts for the sake of custom does not serve, yet he does bow down. You will find such people in Numbers, gratifying women and bowing down to idols.

problems.quote: "Whatever is in heaven above, and whatever is on the earth below, and whatever is in the waters under the earth. You shall not bow down to them, nor shall you serve them" (Exodus 20:4-5).
problems.source_quote: Ὅσα ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ἄνω, καὶ ὅσα ἐν τῇ γῇ κάτω. καὶ ὅσα ἐν τοῖς ὕδασιν ὑποκάτω τῆς γῆς. Οὐ προσκυνήσεις αὐτοῖς, οὐδὲ μὴ λατρεύσεις αὐτοῖς.
problems.why: The quoted passage includes “Whatever is in heaven…”, which is not part of Exodus 20:4‑5; the citation is inaccurate.
problems.fix: Quote the passage without the “Whatever is in heaven…” intro, or cite the correct verse (e.g., Exodus 20:5) for the bowing/serving injunction.
problems.ruling: Source quotes Exodus 20:4-5 content; 'whatever is in heaven' etc. is from 20:4, so citation Exodus 20:4-5 is correct, not wrong.

fixed: The citation is inaccurate: the quoted passage includes 'Whatever is in heaven above…', which is part of Exodus 20:4, not 20:5. Changed the citation to (Exodus 20:4).

problems.why: Greek name 'Arithmoi' in intro but English 'Numbers' in section 20; reader may not connect them.

problems.quote: You will find such people in Numbers
problems.why: Unclear if Origen speaks or quotes Scripture; 'such people' refers back to hypocrites but breaks flow.
'Gratifying' suggests pleasing, but context implies sexual immorality or idolatry with Moabites.
problems.fix: 'indulging with women' or 'whoring with Moabite women'.

problems.quote: a mixed creature from a human and a horse
problems.why: Odd example for an idol; context suggests mythical or composite beings, not a literal centaur.
problems.fix: Clarify this means a fabricated or imaginary composite being, not a real hybrid.

edits.old: You will find such people in Numbers, gratifying women and bowing down to idols.
edits.new: You will find such people in Arithmoi (Numbers), gratifying women and bowing down to idols.

edits.old: a mixed creature from a human and a horse
edits.new: a fabricated composite creature from a human and a horse

fixed: Changed 'Numbers' to 'Arithmoi (Numbers)' to connect the Greek name in the intro with the English name in section 20.
Changed 'gratifying women' to 'indulging with women' to better reflect the context of sexual immorality or idolatry with Moabites, as suggested.
Changed 'a mixed creature' to 'a fabricated composite creature' to clarify that the idol is an imaginary composite being, not a real hybrid, as suggested.
